title: Neurocognitive Integrity After Proton Therapy for Brain Tumor
official: Prospective Evaluation of Neurocognitive Integrity After Proton Therapy for Brain Tumor
summary: Radiation therapy remains a cornerstone in the management of both benign and malignant intracranial tumors, either as monotherapy or combined with surgery and/or chemotherapy. Despite its therapeutic benefits, it is frequently associated with potential long-term adverse effects, with neurotoxicity posing a major challenge, especially in young patients affected by benign primary tumors.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Primary tumors of Brain Tumor (CNS), benign and malignant
* Age ≥ 18 years
* Patients able to speak and read the local language(s) fluently
* Acceptance and signature of informed consent
* Radiological diagnosis, biopsy, or previous surgery
* Concomitant medical therapy is allowed

Exclusion Criteria:

* Previous brain radiotherapy (any form)
* High-grade gliomas
* Patients with concomitant neurological or psychiatric disorders.
* Pregnancy
